name: Sundry
classification_notes: Early 20th-century grotesque revival with humanist warmth. Hand-drawn and hand-cut origins give the design its idiosyncratic character — closed apertures, large x-height, consistently rounded forms — while remaining readable and structurally consistent across three widths.
summary: A warm early 20th-century grotesque revival across three widths and seven weights, its hand-drawn origins kept just legible enough to feel human rather than mechanical.
description: Sundry is J Foundry's interpretation of the early 20th-century grotesque tradition, drawn and cut by hand to preserve the idiosyncrasies and warmth of the originals without sacrificing consistency. The family runs three widths – Standard, Narrow and Condensed – each with seven weights from Thin to Super Black and matching italics, totalling 42 styles plus variable font editions. Large x-height, closed apertures and alternate glyphs (including alternate a and g) make it well-suited to editorial, newspaper and text work where personality is an asset.
foundry_blurb: J Foundry describes Sundry as their take on the early 20th-century grotesque: drawn and cut by hand, these sans serifs carry the idiosyncrasies and quirks of their origins, producing a warm, friendly look. The design evens out those quirks and adds consistency without losing the warmth, aiming to balance character and structure for a clear but personable read.

name: Cutmark
classification_notes: Industrial utility sans-serif with 45° chamfered corners, flattened ink traps and wide apex forms. Three widths (Regular, Condensed, Narrow), 10 weights each with matching italics. Variable font available spanning weight, width and slant axes. OpenType alternates include angled/straight character sets and alternate letterforms.
summary: A utility-first industrial sans with 45° chamfered corners and flattened ink traps, spanning three widths and 60 static styles plus a variable font.
description: Cutmark was designed by Jason Vandenberg at J Foundry in 2021, built around chamfered corners, flattened ink traps and wide apex forms that give it a distinctly mechanical quality. The superfamily covers Regular, Condensed and Narrow widths, each with 10 weights and matching italics for 60 styles in total, alongside a variable font spanning weight, width and slant axes. OpenType alternates include angled and straight character sets, single-storey 'a', hooked 'l' and an alternate 'I' form.
foundry_blurb: Built for function, Cutmark features chamfered corners, flattened ink traps and wide apex forms. Customise the look with alternates including an Angled Set, Straight Set, Beam I, single-storey 'a' and hooked 'l'. The full superfamily covers 60 styles across three widths with matching italics and a variable font.

name: Town
classification_notes: Art Deco-inspired geometric sans-serif superfamily with 12 sub-families covering text, display, chic, contrast, dimensional, inline, lines, shadow, stencil, emboss, and two accent families. Town Text is the only sub-family with italics. Dimensional, Inline, Shadow and Lines sub-families are designed for layering on top of one another. No condensed or extended width variants.
summary: An Art Deco-inspired display superfamily spanning 12 sub-families and 114 styles, built for layering and well-suited to hospitality, food and bespoke brand identities.
description: Designed by Jason Vandenberg, Town draws from Art Deco lettering traditions and scales from text weights with full italics through to dimensional, inline, shadow and stencil variants designed to be layered on top of one another. The 12 sub-families share compatible proportions, making it straightforward to combine styles within a single composition. At 114 styles in total, it covers signage, menus, packaging and editorial work within one cohesive system.
foundry_blurb: J Foundry positions Town as a display collection inspired by Art Deco and contemporary lettering, offering 114 interchangeable and layerable styles across 12 sub-families for use in branding, signage, restaurant menus, packaging and editorial design.

name: Stash
classification_notes: Hand-lettered script modelled on painted signage and brushwork lettering. Two distinct subfamilies share the same underlying construction but differ in surface texture: a clean modern version and a heavily distressed Vintage variant. Often classified alongside formal and display scripts due to its signage character.
summary: A hand-lettered signage script in ten styles — five clean and five distressed vintage — with smart contextual alternates built for craft branding and logotype work.
description: Stash is a script typeface by Jason Vandenberg (2018) drawn from the tradition of painted signage and brushwork lettering. The family splits into two modes — a clean modern variant and a worn Vintage version — each spanning five weights from Light to Black. Contextual alternates manage initial and final forms automatically, while multiple swash lengths, connecting pairs and finishing tails give designers fine control over how crafted the final setting looks.
foundry_blurb: J Foundry pitches Stash for craft beer labels, café logos, packaging and social media content wherever a hand-drawn aesthetic matters. Hundreds of alternate characters mean no two settings look identical, and the Vintage subfamily adds a layer of wear and texture for brands that want an aged, artisanal quality.

name: Mello
classification_notes: A soft, rounded grotesque with consistently curved terminals and corners across all glyphs. Not a geometric or humanist sans – it sits in the grotesque tradition but with a distinctly friendly, approachable character derived from rounded edges rather than geometric construction.
summary: A soft-edged grotesque superfamily in four widths and eight weights, designed for display and branding work that needs warmth without losing authority.
description: Mello is a rounded grotesque by Jason Vandenberg, defined by soft curves and gently rounded corners applied consistently across all 64 styles. The superfamily spans four widths – Standard, Compressed, Condensed and Narrow – each available in eight weights from Thin to Super Black, with italics throughout. Alternate character forms (single-storey 'a', two-storey 'g', rounded 'A', 'R', 'K' and 'y') give art directors options, and an extended Latin character set covers a broad range of European languages.
foundry_blurb: A bold, easy-going grotesque built for display, branding, advertising and packaging. Soft curves and rounded corners give it a warm, approachable character, and the full superfamily of 64 styles – four widths, eight weights, all with italics – gives it the range to carry a whole brand system.

name: Colby
classification_notes: Hand-drawn workhorse sans serif designed to balance the texture and warmth of drawn letterforms with the legibility of a clean geometric sans. Available in six width variants – Compressed through Wide – each with six weights and italics, totalling 72 styles. Sits closer to humanist than geometric despite the hand-drawn DNA.
summary: A hand-drawn workhorse sans spanning six widths and 72 styles, with genuine warmth that holds up from display headings through to body text.
description: Colby by Jason Vandenberg for J Foundry balances the texture of hand-drawn letterforms with the legibility of a clean sans. The family covers six widths – Compressed, Condensed, Narrow, Regular, Extended and Wide – each in six weights with italics. Five stylistic sets, discretionary ligatures, alternate characters and a slashed zero give designers control over how much character they let through.
foundry_blurb: Colby is a hand-drawn workhorse sans serif that balances quirky drawn letterforms with clean sans legibility, offering authentic warmth with functional benefits. It ships with alternates, icons and arrows, making it a natural fit for packaging, restaurant menus, children's books and digital applications.

name: Marsden
classification_notes: A geometric Grotesque with strong display character. Eight-width system from Slim to Wide; condensed forms use flat sides and subtle curves, wider forms open into rounded sides and open curves. Twelve weights from Hairline to Super Black. Marsden Text subfamily adjusts spacing and weights for smaller applications. Italics available in the Text subfamily only.
summary: A no-nonsense geometric Grotesque spanning eight widths and twelve weights, built for display, branding and packaging work that needs a strong, confident voice.
description: Marsden is a geometric Grotesque superfamily by Jason Vandenberg of J Foundry. Eight widths run from Slim to Wide, with condensed forms using flat sides and subtle curves, and wider forms opening into rounded sides and open curves. A rich set of stylistic alternates covers single-story a, two-story g, raised vertex M, rounded G, and straight-tail Q among others, each addressable as an individual style set. Marsden Text extends the system with adjusted weights and spacing for small-size use.
foundry_blurb: J Foundry bills Marsden as a bold, no-nonsense Grotesque for display, branding, advertising and packaging wherever a strong voice is needed. Built on a geometric foundation with enough warmth to keep the style confident and lively, the eight widths and twelve weights flow from condensed to wide with deliberate design intent – completed by a Text subfamily tuned for smaller applications.

name: Abrade
classification_notes: Rational geometric sans-serif with a medium x-height. Futura-influenced in its geometry but distinctly contemporary in its functional refinements. Italics maintain the geometric register rather than switching to cursive forms, preserving the rational character across the full family.
summary: A rational geometric sans-serif from Jason Vandenberg spanning 12 weights with full italic coverage and support for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic.
description: Abrade is a geometric sans-serif designed by Jason Vandenberg and released through J Foundry in 2015. Its medium x-height and classically rational forms hold up at both display and text sizes, making it useful across corporate identity, editorial and digital product work. The 24-style family runs from Hairline to Ultra Black, each weight paired with a geometric italic, plus variable font versions for both upright and italic axes.
foundry_blurb: Abrade brings rational geometry to contemporary use: a geometric sans-serif with a medium x-height that reads well at display and text scales alike. Twelve weights and matching italics, extended Latin, Greek and Cyrillic coverage, and a full OpenType suite – small caps, stylistic alternates, multiple figure sets, fractions, slashed zero and case-sensitive forms – make it a practical choice for publications, digital products and brand systems.

name: Bodoni Sans
classification_notes: Didone-inspired high-contrast sans-serif. Letterforms adapt Bodoni's classical capital proportions and x-heights for sans-serif use rather than simply removing serifs. Three optical sizes – Standard (12–60pt), Display (48pt+) and Text (6–12pt) – each carry distinct contrast adjustments. No condensed variants. Full italic across Standard and Display; Text carries two uprights and two italics only.
summary: A high-contrast sans-serif that adapts Bodoni's classical proportions across three optical sizes, aimed squarely at fashion and editorial use.
description: Bodoni Sans reworks the sharp contrast and elegant geometry of the historic Bodoni serif into a sans-serif form. Jason Vandenberg rebalanced the letterforms rather than simply stripping serifs, and drew an entirely new Light weight to extend the range. Three optical sizes – Standard, Display and Text – each carry adjusted contrast ratios for their intended point-size range, making the family workable from 6pt body copy up to large-format display headings.
foundry_blurb: J Foundry positions Bodoni Sans as a new classic built on two centuries of typographic history: fresh and contemporary while retaining the sophistication associated with the original serif, and tested extensively across web formats for both print and screen.

name: Grey Sans
classification_notes: Angular grotesque sans-serif with geometric construction. Eight weights from Hairline to Black; no italic or condensed cuts. Originally released under the Greyscale Type imprint in 2013, now sold via J Foundry. Character set includes standard ligatures. The angular terminals distinguish it from softer neo-grotesques.
summary: Grey Sans is a geometric grotesque by Jason Vandenberg with sharply angular character, spanning eight weights from Hairline to Black.
description: Designed in 2013 under Vandenberg's Greyscale Type imprint and now sold through J Foundry, Grey Sans takes a clean grotesque structure and cuts it with angular terminals and joints that give it an assertive edge. The eight-weight range – Hairline through Black – makes it adaptable across display headlines, branding and digital interfaces. There are no italic or condensed cuts; the family is deliberately lean.
foundry_blurb: J Foundry describes Grey Sans as a grotesque with an angular design, marketed as an eight-style family for desktop, web and app use across more than 20 languages.

name: Fourth
classification_notes: Contemporary connected roundhand script drawing on classic Americana sources – baseball lettering, sign painting and vintage branding. Described by the foundry as "rational and refined," prioritising consistency and legibility across weights rather than expressive irregularity. No upright roman or italic companion; the script weight axis runs from Thin to Ultra Black.
summary: A contemporary roundhand script in seven weights, rooted in baseball lettering and sign painting, with a full suite of alternates, swash capitals and ornamental extras for branding work.
description: Fourth takes the connected letterforms of classic American roundhand and sharpens them for modern branding and display use. Seven weights from Thin to Ultra Black are supported by contextual alternates for clean joins, stylistic alternates for common letters, swash capitals, catchwords and a separate ornament pack. It is well-suited to sports identities, logos and any project that wants a confident handmade feel without sacrificing legibility.
foundry_blurb: J Foundry positions Fourth as a contemporary roundhand script inspired by baseball scripts, sign painting and classic Americana branding, with rational and refined forms built for consistency across the full weight range.
